title: Do More Modalities Always Help? A Geometric Perspective on Missing-Modality Robustness
abstract: arXiv:2610.04792v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Missing modality remains a longstanding challenge in multimodal learning. Existing methods typically address this issue through modality recovery or adaptive strategies. However, they overlook models' internal cross-modal dependencies formed during multimodal training, which later impair robustness. We systematically characterize a counterintuitive deployment-time failure mode: models trained on full modalities can underperform unimodal models when one modality is missing at inference time. This pattern appears across diverse architectures, such as fusion models, CLIP-style two-tower models, and vision-language models. We show that such degradation is closely associated with learned cross-modal dependencies in the principal parameter subspaces. translated_title: 模态越多总是越好吗？缺失模态鲁棒性的几何视角
translated_abstract: 缺失模态一直是多模态学习中一个长期存在的挑战。现有方法通常通过模态恢复或自适应策略来应对这一问题，但它们忽视了模型在多模态训练过程中形成的内部跨模态依赖关系，而这些依赖会损害模型的鲁棒性。我们系统地刻画了一种反直觉的部署阶段失效模式：在全模态上训练的模型，在推理时缺失某一模态的情况下，其表现可能不如单模态模型。这一模式出现在多种架构中，例如融合模型、CLIP 式双塔模型以及视觉-语言模型。我们证明这种性能下降与主参数子空间中学习到的跨模态依赖密切相关：多模态训练会使这些子空间发生结构化旋转，尤其是在跨模态交互层中，而这些旋转与任务对齐余量的减小以及更大的……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文揭示了一种反直觉现象——在全模态上训练的模型在推理时缺失某个模态可能不如单模态模型，其几何根源在于多模态训练导致主参数子空间发生结构化旋转并形成有害的跨模态依赖。
en_tdlr: Models trained on full modalities can underperform unimodal models when a modality is missing at inference time, and this degradation is geometrically tied to structured rotations of principal parameter subspaces induced by learned cross-modal dependencies during multimodal training.
